drhp.business: Marine Electricals (India) provides power generation and distribution, automation, integrated monitoring and control, navigation/communication (NAVCOM) and integrated bridge systems to the Indian Navy, shipbuilders and marine customers, and critical power and power-distribution/automation solutions to data centres and industrial infrastructure. The Industry segment accounts for approximately 65% of its order backlog. Through subsidiaries it offers EV charging solutions (Evigo Charge) and has foreign subsidiaries located in the UAE, Canada and Italy.
drhp.end_markets: Indian Navy / defence|Shipbuilding and marine|Public sector undertakings dealing in shipping|Data centres|Industrial infrastructure|Power distribution and automation|Ports and coastal surveillance|Electric mobility (EV charging)|Overseas via subsidiaries in UAE, Canada (Kelowna, British Columbia) and Italy
drhp.expansion: No plant, capacity or capex project is described in this bundle. The only expansion narrative is the Chairman's statement of 'continued expansion of our product portfolio' and 'ability to offer a broader range of solutions', which management expects to strengthen the order book in FY 2026-27.
drhp.mdna: Navy expansion: Make in India has accelerated indigenisation in shipbuilding and the vision of a 200-ship combat fleet by 2035 is cited as a catalyst for naval expansion; the Indian Navy anchors the defence and marine businesses.|Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy (SBFAP) subsidies aim to make Indian shipyards competitive and position India among the top five shipbuilding nations by 2047.|Data-centre build-out: footprint of ~16 million sq. ft. in 2025 expected to reach ~55 million sq. ft. over the next 5-6 years, helped by infrastructure status and data-localisation policy.|Power-sector electrification and clean-energy transition align with the company's power distribution and automation offerings.|EV adoption accelerating on fuel costs, climate imperatives and subsidies, supporting the Evigo charging business.|Maritime safety and efficiency as national priorities; management expects maritime domain awareness to become a strong contributor to growth.|FY26 improvement attributed to better volumes, improved product mix and cost savings.|Headwinds flagged: evolving global tariff regimes and geopolitical tensions, including the West Asia conflict, disrupting supply chains and capital flows.|Order book reached approximately Rs. 12,546 million at end-FY26 versus Rs. 5,240 million in FY 2024-25, an increase of nearly 139% year-on-year.|The Industry segment accounts for approximately 65% of the order backlog, driven by Data Centres and Industrial Infrastructure.|Management anticipates further strengthening of the order book during FY 2026-27.|Credit ratings factor in the healthy order book providing adequate near-term revenue visibility.

Per the Ken Research Report the India Dies and Moulds Market was valued at INR 45,400 crore in FY'25 and is projected to grow at an 11.5% CAGR to FY'30F, with Automotive Moulds the largest application at INR 25.2 thousand crore in FY'25 and B2B/OEM the dominant distribution channel. Demand is presented as being pulled by India's industrial and infrastructure cycle - Union …

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Indian Navy / defence
- Shipbuilding and marine
- Public sector undertakings dealing in shipping
- Data centres
- Industrial infrastructure
- Power distribution and automation
- Ports and coastal surveillance
- Electric mobility (EV charging)
- Overseas via subsidiaries in UAE, Canada (Kelowna, British Columbia) and Italy

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Navy expansion: Make in India has accelerated indigenisation in shipbuilding and the vision of a 200-ship combat fleet by 2035 is cited as a catalyst for naval expansion; the Indian Navy anchors the defence and marine businesses.
- Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy (SBFAP) subsidies aim to make Indian shipyards competitive and position India among the top five shipbuilding nations by 2047.
- Data-centre build-out: footprint of ~16 million sq. ft. in 2025 expected to reach ~55 million sq. ft. over the next 5-6 years, helped by infrastructure status and data-localisation policy.
- Power-sector electrification and clean-energy transition align with the company's power distribution and automation offerings.
- EV adoption accelerating on fuel costs, climate imperatives and subsidies, supporting the Evigo charging business.
- Maritime safety and efficiency as national priorities; management expects maritime domain awareness to become a strong contributor to growth.
- FY26 improvement attributed to better volumes, improved product mix and cost savings.
- Headwinds flagged: evolving global tariff regimes and geopolitical tensions, including the West Asia conflict, disrupting supply chains and capital flows.
- Order book reached approximately Rs. 12,546 million at end-FY26 versus Rs. 5,240 million in FY 2024-25, an increase of nearly 139% year-on-year.
- The Industry segment accounts for approximately 65% of the order backlog, driven by Data Centres and Industrial Infrastructure.
- Management anticipates further strengthening of the order book during FY 2026-27.
- Credit ratings factor in the healthy order book providing adequate near-term revenue visibility.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: No plant, capacity or capex project is described in this bundle. The only expansion narrative is the Chairman's statement of 'continued expansion of our product portfolio' and 'ability to offer a broader range of solutions', which management expects to strengthen the order book in FY 2026-27.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Focus on R&D, indigenisation, innovation and fiscal discipline to sustain growth and strengthen the order book.
- Continue expanding the product portfolio to offer customers a broader range of solutions across Marine & Defence, Power Distribution, EV Charging and Data Centres.
- Serve naval indigenisation and shipbuilding demand with Integrated Bridge Systems, NAVCOM, power generation/distribution, integrated monitoring & control, electric/battery propulsion and integrated communication solutions.
- Deepen critical-power supply to large-scale data centres and industrial infrastructure.
- Build maritime domain awareness business (coastal surveillance, port management, vessel traffic systems), in which the company says it has invested significantly.
- Grow EV charging through subsidiary Evigo Charge across homes, workplaces, fleets and e-bus, while exploring two- and three-wheeler charging; new collaborations with government agencies and private players formed during the year.
- Converted Marks Marine Radio Private Limited into a subsidiary by acquiring an additional 10% stake (49.25% to 59.20%) on 12 May 2025.

themes.title: Naval shipbuilding & maritime
themes.need: A multi-decade naval order book and indigenous warship/submarine build, plus the naval-equipment supply chain (HVAC/chillers, mechanical seals, marine gearing) and maritime services, underpin the theme. GRSE carries a large RFP pipeline (~INR1.5 lakh cr referenced); SHREE REFRIGERATIONS 544458 supplies naval HVAC; SEALMATIC 543782 naval/submarine seals; ELECON defence-marine gearing; KMEW/SEAMECLTD/DREDGECORP maritime services.
themes.driver: Fresh MoD warship/submarine orders + naval-equipment indigenization inflow; maritime-infra/offshore contract wins.

hero.oneLiner: Integrated electrical, automation, navigation and communication systems supplier anchored by the Indian Navy and defence/marine business, with a growing industry (data-centre and industrial infrastructure) franchise and EV charging through its subsidiary Evigo Charge.
